correctness.rationale: For Q_j=exp(tau_j(beta A_j-mu I)), each Q_j is symmetric invertible. Three-factor permutations are generated by cyclic product similarity and reversal transpose, preserving the full spectrum. For n<=2 every undirected loopless adjacency is a scalar multiple of the sole edge matrix. At n=3, direct multiplication of E_12,E_23,E_13 with hyperbolic block [5/4,3/4] yields rational M_adj and M_sep; independent exact-rational checks confirmed charpolys and strict Perron comparisons M_adj*(16,11,16)>7*(16,11,16) and M_sep*(16,11,14)<7*(16,11,14). With e^(-4mu)=1/7 these are strict super/subcritical monodromies. Cooperative order-preserving SIS map, positivity of the period map and strict subhomogeneity give uniqueness and global attraction of positive fixed point; subcritical comparison P(x)<=U x gives exponential extinction. These arguments apply to all finite n and durations attached to symmetric snapshots, not just checked four-edge examples.

originality.rationale: Three-factor spectral equality follows from elementary symmetric product identities and cannot be claimed as a novel general matrix theorem. The surviving mathematical assertion is the sharp minimal phase/node budget with exact threshold-changing identical-exposure schedules and nonlinear outcome. The inspected two-phase Floquet and graph-commutator literature does not present the sharp three-versus-four threshold.

Nonlinear global attraction requires all snapshot union edges active during a period; this holds for the specified A,B,C witness but not asserted generically.
